newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-VLADIKAVKAZ NEW FAVOURITES TO KEEP RUSSIAN TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VLADIKAVKAZ NEW FAVOURITES TO KEEP RUSSIAN TITLE.

text.p: Alania Vladikavkaz went top of the Russian league on Friday after an unexpected slip by main challengers Spartak Moscow and are now favourites to retain their title on the last day of the season.

Alania, who have trailed Spartak and outsiders Rotor Volgograd for much of the season, won 2-0 at already relegated Tekstilshchik Kamyshin while Spartak needed an 85th minute goal to secure a 1-1 home draw against mid-table Rostselmash Rostov.

Both sides are on 69 points but Bakhva Tedeyev's goals in the 37th and 87th minutes put Alania top because they have one more win. They also appear to have the easiest closing fixture on November 3 when they play Lokomotiv Nizhny Novgorod at home.
Spartak face a difficult away tie at Zenit St Petersburg, whose coach Pavel Sadyrin detests the Moscow side and inspired his team to a fine 2-0 away win over them in July.
Rotor, leaders before last weekend's games, stumbled again by losing 2-0 at Lokomotiv Moscow and stay on 67 points, dropping to third place.
They face struggling Uralmash Yekaterinburg next week but can only win the title in the unlikely event of both Spartak and Alania losing.
Spartak started the day in top spot, knowing they could virtually clinch the title if second-placed Rotor lost.
The Moscow team -- who won the Russian championship three years in a row from 1992 to 1994 -- attacked from the start but were defied by their opponents' rugged defence and the woodwork.

Spartak looked down and out in the 83rd minute when veteran defender Sergei Gorlukovich conceded a free-kick 20 metres out and Rostselmash midfielder Alexei Gerasimenko scored with a beautiful curling shot into the top corner.

Spartak pushed forward and two minutes later were awarded a free-kick on the edge of the box. Rostselmash expected a blasted shot but were undone when Gorlukovich chipped the ball gently over the wall into the net to atone for his earlier error.
Rotor have been in reverse gear over the last few weeks and their defeat at Lokomotiv came as no surprise with Ukrainian striker Oleg Garas netting in the 20th and 86th minutes.
Last week, Rotor lost two crucial points in a 0-0 draw at struggling Chernomorets Novorossiisk and then accused a linesman of being drunk after he had ruled out a goal.
But Chernomorets showed the result was no fluke by pulling off a stunning 3-1 win at fourth-placed CSKA Moscow, who until last week had an outside chance of the title.
Lada Togliatti and Tekstilshchik are already relegated and the third team to join them looks likely to be Uralmash, who lost 2-0 to Dynamo Moscow.

The Yekaterinburg side face the wrath of Rotor next week while KamAZ Naberzhnye Chelny are away to Rostselmash. If both sides lose KamAZ will stay up because they have recorded one more win than their rivals.
